verified_mandate.notes: Exhaustive search of JDIH Kemenhub (Ministry of Transportation regulation database), kemenhub.go.id, dephub.go.id, kominfo.go.id, komdigi.go.id, Indonesia.go.id, ALFI/ILFA association site, and full-text web searches in both English and Bahasa Indonesia returned zero government publications referencing an ePOD mandate. The Kemkominfo citation surfaced by Mordor Intelligence ('Kemkominfo Dorong Implementasi e-POD Logistik Nasional') is unverifiable: no such document appears on jdih.komdigi.go.id, kominfo.go.id, or any indexed government page. Mordor Intelligence market reports are secondary/commercial and known to include unverifiable AI-generated policy summaries. Kemkomdigi did publish Permenkominfo No. 8/2025 on commercial postal services, but it addresses postal licensing, not a mandatory ePOD rollout with a Q3 2026 enforcement deadline.

fraud_loss_figure.notes: The IDR 2.1 trillion ($130M) figure for logistics delivery-receipt fraud appears only in: (1) the original blog.cfglobal.co post (unverified industry consultancy blog, no citation chain provided), and (2) Mordor Intelligence's Indonesia e-commerce logistics market report which itself cites 'Kemkominfo Dorong Implementasi e-POD Logistik Nasional' — a document that cannot be located on any official Indonesian government portal. BPS statistics, OJK fraud reports, and Indonesian financial crime data reference fraud losses in financial services, banking, and online scams (IDR 4.6T–9.1T ranges) but none are logistics-POD-fraud specific. The IDR 2.1T figure is unverifiable and likely fabricated or misattributed.

notes: ATTENDED-FETCH NEEDED: kemenhub.go.id returns a server-level rejection ('URL was rejected') in automated fetches. A logged-in or browser-rendered fetch of https://www.dephub.go.id/ search for 'ePOD' or 'bukti pengiriman elektronik' is recommended to definitively rule out any unpublicized directive. Additionally, the ALFI member portal (members-only circulars at alfi.or.id) and the Kemkomdigi internal communications archive may contain draft policy documents not indexed publicly. The Mordor Intelligence citation chain — which is the only secondary source that echoes the IDR 2.1T figure — traces back to a named-but-unfindable government document, a hallmark pattern of AI-hallucinated citations in commercial market reports. Verdict: the claim as written should be dropped from the artifact unless attended-mode verification of Kemenhub and ALFI member archives produces a government document.
